consensus: Bracket-3 Edgar in late 2026 is a lord-dense Vampire swarm that wins by combat with a drain rider, not a drain deck with Vampires as fuel. EDHREC's 'Upgraded' (bracket 3) filter holds 5,876 self-tagged decks, averages 35 lands and 34 creatures, and its top ten is lords and cheap Vampire bodies: Captivating Vampire 87.1%, Cordial Vampire 85.9%, Blood Artist 85.6%, Welcoming Vampire 79.1%, Stromkirk Captain 76.6%, Indulgent Aristocrat 75.9%, Bloodline Keeper 74.7%, Legion Lieutenant 71.7%, Sanctum Seeker 71.1%, Swords to Plowshares 71.0%. Its non-combat reach is Sanctum Seeker (71.1%), Vito (67.0%), Malakir Bloodwitch (55.0%), Bloodletter of Aclazotz (45.4%) and Sanguine Bond (41.6%); Bloodthirsty Conqueror (52.8%) and Exquisite Blood (48.6%) are still run by half of bracket-3 lists even though Nerd Leagues (Oct 2026) names the Blood/Bond pair as what 'gets Vampire decks asked to leave bracket 3 pods'. Its refills are Vampire-count burst draw (Champion of Dusk 47.3%, Pact of the Serpent 29.4%) plus Skullclamp (68.4%) and Village Rites (34.7%); its wipes are one-sided (Olivia's Wrath 59.3%, Damn 29.4%); its protection is a thin two or three (Teferi's Protection 30.9%, Boros Charm 29.3%, Akroma's Will 23.1%); its ramp is five or six rocks with Dark Ritual (33.2%). Against that, the threat-v1 branch (35 lands, 29 Vampire creatures, three rocks) is heavier on per-death drain, protection and sacrifice recursion than any published list and lighter on lords, Vampire-count draw, one-sided wipes and rocks. No fetchable primer describes a bracket-3 Edgar built as the pilot describes; the closest filter is EDHREC's Upgraded + Aristocrats (524 decks) and Upgraded + Lifedrain (87 decks), and both still run the loop pieces.

findings.claim: The bracket-3 consensus core is lords. Of the eight Vampire lords/pseudo-lords above 50% in the 5,876-deck Upgraded filter, the branch runs three (Cordial Vampire, Bloodline Keeper, Master of Dark Rites) and lacks five: Captivating Vampire 87.1% (5,117), Stromkirk Captain 76.6% (4,500), Indulgent Aristocrat 75.9% (4,462), Legion Lieutenant 71.7% (4,211), Markov Baron 52.4% (3,077, a 'High Lift' card). Walser (Draftsim, May 2026) ranks the lords #2 of 28: 'lords are a must-include to make the wide board threatening', Captivating Vampire best; Indulgent Aristocrat 'is weaker than a proper lord but still useful'. Nerd Leagues runs five lords and calls them the deck's anthem sources. This is combat-plan evidence and it collides with the pilot's standing rule that a flat +1/+1 is too slow; recorded as what the strong lists do, not as a recommendation.

The most-run non-combat finisher in bracket 3 is one the branch does not have: Sanctum Seeker, 71.1% of Upgraded decks (4,180/5,876), 69.1% of Upgraded Aristocrats (362/524), 66.7% of Upgraded Lifedrain (58/87). Nerd Leagues lists it among its win conditions ('drains each opponent for 1 per attacking Vampire'); Walser ranks it #13, 'like a lord on a different axis, since creatures don't need to connect for damage to go through'. With Bloodletter of Aclazotz (45.4%) already in the branch each attack trigger is doubled. Malakir Bloodwitch is the second: 55.0% Upgraded (3,233), 58.6% Upgraded Lifedrain, Walser #3 (its ETB 'applies the heat' and breaks board stalls), Furtado (Oct 2026) 'an instant win card if your board state is big enough'. Vengeful Bloodwitch is the cheap per-death drain the bracket-3 aristocrats lists added since the last recon: 46.4% of Upgraded Aristocrats (243/524), in the average 99, Roberts (Mar 2026) 'a slam dunk into Edgar Markov decks' because it is a Vampire that triggers eminence where Zulaport does not. Kalastria Highborn is Nerd Leagues' fourth drain body (pay B on a Vampire death: drain 2, doubled by Bloodletter) and is below EDHREC's visible cut.

Running out of cards is answered in the strong lists by Vampire-count burst draw, which the branch has none of. Champion of Dusk: 47.3% Upgraded (2,777), 50.0% Upgraded Aristocrats; Walser #12, it 'converts a massive board into a ton of card draw' and is Pact of the Serpent 'on a stick'; Nerd Leagues: 'count before casting' because the eminence tokens inflate the life cost. Pact of the Serpent: 29.4% Upgraded (1,726), 33.0% Upgraded Aristocrats, Walser #4 'one of the greatest typal payoffs in black'. Village Rites (34.7%, 2,037) is the instant-speed response to a wipe and is in the average bracket-3 aristocrats 99. Phyrexian Arena (29.5%) and Herald's Horn (32.3%, in the average 99) are the steady engines. The token-draw pieces the pilot is weighing are minority picks with no Edgar-specific write-up anywhere fetched: Idol of Oblivion 17.6% Upgraded (1,036), 18.3% Upgraded Aristocrats; Deadly Dispute 17.8% (1,046), 24.0% Upgraded Aristocrats; Bennie Bracks, Zoologist is below EDHREC's visible cut in every filter and no fetched source mentions it with Edgar.

The strong lists wipe one-sidedly; the branch's two sweepers (Toxic Deluge 10.2% Upgraded, The Meathook Massacre 20.8% Upgraded Aristocrats) are symmetric. Olivia's Wrath is the archetype's sweeper at 59.3% Upgraded (3,484), 60.3% Upgraded Aristocrats, 62.1% Upgraded Lifedrain; Walser #6; Nerd Leagues: 'a one-sided wrath that gets bigger the longer the game goes'. Damn 29.4% (1,725): Nerd Leagues' line is Boros Charm indestructible first, then overload 'as a wrath that only hits opponents'. Ruinous Ultimatum is in the average bracket-3 aristocrats 99 and Nerd Leagues' list; Kindred Dominance 17.0% (1,000), Walser #11 'throws a typal board wipe at the wall'. Everything Comes to Dust is 5.1% Upgraded (302) with no write-up; Winds of Abandon is below the visible cut in every filter — neither is a card the strong lists reach for.

On protection the branch is already above consensus, not below it. Bracket-3 lists run two or three: Teferi's Protection 30.9% (1,815), Boros Charm 29.3% (1,721), Akroma's Will 23.1% (1,355), and the average bracket-3 aristocrats 99 carries exactly Teferi's and Boros Charm. The branch runs all three plus Selfless Spirit and Giver of Runes (neither listed in any filter). Of the cards the pilot is weighing: Clever Concealment is 11.0% Upgraded (645), 13.9% Upgraded Aristocrats, but Walser's 'go-to' protection 'since phasing counters sweepers and bounce' and it convokes off tokens; Guardian of Faith and Lethal Scheme are below the visible cut in every filter with no Edgar write-up; Reconnaissance is 5.2% (303), named by Walser only in passing beside Sanctum Seeker and by Perry (CoolStuffInc, 2025) as a threat to watch. Recovery rather than prevention is the other school: Walser #16 Patriarch's Bidding and Bloodline Bidding are 'the next best thing to rebuild after' a wipe; Roberts: Bloodline Bidding convokes cheaply and will 'bring back our creatures, should we get wiped'; Nerd Leagues calls Teferi's 'the best answer this deck has to a wrath' and Purphoros 'the one piece of the engine no wrath touches'.

Land count 34–36 and five or six rocks is the consensus; the branch's 35 lands is inside it and its three rocks (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Orzhov Signet) is under it. EDHREC averages: 36 lands overall (15 basic/21 nonbasic), 35 Upgraded (13/22), 35 Upgraded Aristocrats (11/24), 36 Upgraded Lifedrain. Nerd Leagues 34 lands and 'five mana rocks'; Furtado 34 lands and six rocks; argas' Upgraded list 35; Decklab's bracket-2 list 37 with ten rocks. The average bracket-3 aristocrats 99 runs Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Orzhov Signet, Talisman of Hierarchy (35.7% Upgraded), Talisman of Indulgence, Herald's Horn and Dark Ritual (33.2%). The typal lands the strong lists run and the branch lacks: Three Tree City 32.3% (1,899), Furtado 'awesome in a typal deck that wants to go wide', 'typically turn 2 mana into 5 or 6', Roberts 'a great card for Vampire decks'; Vault of the Archangel 37.2% (2,185) and Path of Ancestry, Unclaimed Territory, Secluded Courtyard, Cavern of Souls, Voldaren Estate are in the average 99. The branch runs Phyrexian Tower (29.1%) and Castle Locthwain (11.3%).

Spot removal: the count matches, the cards do not. The average bracket-3 aristocrats 99 runs Swords 71.8%, Path to Exile 53.8%, Anguished Unmaking 50.6%, Damn, Olivia's Wrath, Ruinous Ultimatum and Ruthless Lawbringer 37.4% (29.8% Upgraded; Roberts 'spot removal with fangs!', a Vampire that eats a token to destroy a nonland permanent). The branch's Crackling Doom (12.0% Upgraded, 6.9% Upgraded Aristocrats) and Vanishing Verse (below the visible cut) are off-consensus picks; Path to Exile at 51.2% is the consensus second white exile the branch lacks. Perry's reading of why Edgar loses is the counter-evidence for stack interaction: Mardu 'is notoriously bad at interacting with spells on the stack', so the strong lists spend on creature and permanent removal, not on more.

Bracket traps the strong lists still run and this deck must not. Bloodthirsty Conqueror is 52.8% of bracket-3 lists (3,104) and Roberts calls it 'Perhaps one of the best Vampires to come out in the last two years', but it is Exquisite Blood on a body: with Vito or Sanguine Bond (both in the branch) it is the two-card infinite the pilot's rule makes bracket 4, and Nerd Leagues only keeps it by 'agreeing with the pod in advance not to tutor for the second piece'. Exquisite Blood 48.6% is the same pair. Phyrexian Altar is in the average bracket-3 aristocrats 99 (26.7%, 140/524) and Commander Spellbook's most popular Edgar line (popularity 5,085) is Edgar Markov + Oathsworn Vampire + Phyrexian Altar with Edgar in the command zone — the branch runs Oathsworn Vampire, so Altar would be a commander-inclusive two-card line. Warren Soultrader forms Edgar + Oathsworn + Soultrader + Blood Artist (popularity 1,194), three cards in the 99. None of these is a recommendation; the branch's own five contained lines (none two-card, per deck-facts) are a separate matter for resolve-stack.

The pilot's remaining weighed cards, with what the strong lists say — which is mostly a number and no prose. Shared Animosity 38.7% Upgraded (2,275), 36.8% Upgraded Aristocrats, in the average 99 and Nerd Leagues' combat win conditions ('a seven-creature attack gives +6 to each'); a combat finisher that scales with attackers, which fits the pilot's multiply-or-scale rule and not the non-combat thesis. Roaming Throne 14.6% (856), 20.7% Upgraded Lifedrain, not listed in Upgraded Aristocrats: its oracle text doubles 'a triggered ability of another creature you control of the chosen type', so it does NOT double eminence (Edgar in the command zone is not a creature you control) and does nothing to Bloodletter's replacement effect; it doubles Edgar's attack trigger on the battlefield and Vampire triggers like Blood Artist, Sanctum Seeker and Bloodwitch's ETB. Bartolomé del Presidio 25.4% Upgraded, 40.5% Upgraded Aristocrats, in the average 99, no write-up fetched. Falkenrath Pit Fighter 23.4%, a 'High Lift' card; Walser #10 groups the one-mana Vampires as 'critical curve savers'. Edgar, Charmed Groom 55.3% (3,249), in the average 99 and Nerd Leagues' list, no judgment fetched. Legion's Landing 19.4%; Nerd Leagues runs it. Patron of the Vein 35.3% but Nerd Leagues cut it: a six-drop 'still in your hand when the game is decided'; Furtado keeps it for removal on ETB. Vampire Nocturnus 19.7%, a 'High Lift' card; Furtado 'grants evasion if the top card of your library is black' — 47 of the branch's 99 copies carry black on the front face (cards.csv colors; lands are colourless). Black Market Connections 29.0%, in the average 99 and the branch already.

Slow kindred artifacts are minority picks in bracket 3 and the branch runs one. Herald's Horn is the one the lists keep (32.3% Upgraded, in the average 99; Roberts' answer to Horn versus Gathering Stone is 'Why not both?'). Vanquisher's Banner 26.2% — Nerd Leagues cut it for Intangible Virtue; Urza's Incubator 13.5% (794), 10.5% Upgraded Aristocrats — the branch runs it and no fetched source endorses it for Edgar (Furtado lists it only as 'upwards of $10'); Door of Destinies 14.9%, Coat of Arms 10.7%. Nerd Leagues' Intangible Virtue and Walser's On Wings of Gold / All-Out Assault are the flat-anthem school; against it, Walser's Warleader's Call ranks #19 because it 'adds damage and carries an anthem' and Impact Tremors (26.9% Upgraded Aristocrats, in the average 99) is the non-combat ETB payoff that reads every eminence token.

known_failure_modes: Running out of gas. Perry (CoolStuffInc, Mar 2025): like most aggro decks Edgar 'struggles with running out of gas', since these colours lack strong card draw; the strong lists answer it with Vampire-count burst draw (Champion of Dusk, Pact of the Serpent) and Skullclamp, which Nerd Leagues calls 'the single best play in the deck' and Walser 'can't imagine building the deck without'.

Combat dependence. Perry: 'The deck also relies entirely on combat', so board-control and non-combat opponents trouble it; his answers are Crawlspace, Inkshield and Pestilence (which 'kills the 1/1 Vampires as they appear'). The bracket-3 lists' non-combat reach is Sanctum Seeker, Vito/Bond, Bloodwitch's ETB, Impact Tremors/Purphoros — none of which needs a creature to connect.

The wipe. Decklab (Oct 2026): 'Board wipes are the second risk, although eminence lets you rebuild with tokens'; Nerd Leagues: Teferi's Protection is 'the best answer this deck has to a wrath' and Purphoros 'the one piece of the engine no wrath touches'; Walser: the Biddings are 'the next best thing to rebuild after' one. Furtado dissents: 'you can get back online pretty quickly after one' because the deck holds back generators and anthems.

Stack blindness. Perry: Mardu 'is notoriously bad at interacting with spells on the stack', so a non-combat win such as Exsanguinate beats it; no bracket-3 list fetched runs a counter-equivalent beyond Teferi's Protection and phasing.

The bracket trap. Nerd Leagues: the Exquisite Blood + Sanguine Bond pair 'gets Vampire decks asked to leave bracket 3 pods', and Bloodthirsty Conqueror 'carries Exquisite Blood's text'; half of self-tagged bracket-3 lists still run Conqueror (52.8%) and Exquisite Blood (48.6%), so the tag is not a guarantee of what a bracket-3 Edgar pod expects.

Being the target. Perry's advice to opponents is to avoid being 'the player who slams an early Sol Ring and becomes Edgar's first target' and to look for a board wipe, since once 'the board is cleared and hands are low, your individual card quality should pull you ahead' — the hand-empty-after-the-wipe state is the one the strong lists build against.
contested: Lords versus scaling payoffs. Every fetched list and Walser's ranking treat five to eight lords as mandatory ('a must-include'); the pilot's standing rule is that a flat +1/+1 is too slow and only multiplying or scaling effects earn a slot. Recon records the consensus; diagnose decides against this deck's measured axes.

Prevention versus recovery after a wipe. Teferi's/Boros Charm/Akroma's Will (Nerd Leagues, the average 99) against Patriarch's Bidding/Bloodline Bidding (Walser, Roberts) against 'eminence rebuilds' (Decklab, Furtado). The branch is already heavier on prevention than any list fetched.

Whether Bloodthirsty Conqueror belongs in bracket 3. 52.8% of self-tagged bracket-3 lists run it; Nerd Leagues keeps it on a table agreement; the pilot's rule (two-card infinite = bracket 4) excludes it while Vito or Sanguine Bond is in the 99.
Patron of the Vein: 35.3% inclusion and Furtado's 'removal on ETB' against Nerd Leagues cutting it as a six-drop 'still in your hand when the game is decided'.
Kindred artifacts: Herald's Horn kept by the average 99, Vanquisher's Banner cut by Nerd Leagues, Urza's Incubator at 13.5% with no endorsement fetched.

Symmetric versus one-sided sweepers: the branch's Toxic Deluge and Meathook Massacre are run by 10–21% of bracket-3 lists; Olivia's Wrath by 59%. With Blood Artist, Zulaport, Bastion, Falkenrath Noble and Meathook in the branch, a symmetric wipe is also a drain event — no fetched source weighs that trade for Edgar.

EDHREC bracket tags are self-reported and cover 13,889 of 52,819 decks; the 'Upgraded' filter is 5,876 decks that call themselves bracket 3, half of which still run Bloodthirsty Conqueror or Exquisite Blood. 'Not listed' in any EDHREC figure means below the page's visible cut (the JSON truncates at ~50 cards per type and the fetch at 100,000 characters), not zero — this applies to Bennie Bracks, Guardian of Faith, Lethal Scheme, Winds of Abandon, Zulaport Cutthroat, Kalastria Highborn, Vanishing Verse, Selfless Spirit, Giver of Runes and the branch's other off-list cards.

No fetched source gives a card-specific Edgar judgment for Roaming Throne, Idol of Oblivion, Bennie Bracks, Deadly Dispute, Bartolomé del Presidio, Guardian of Faith, Lethal Scheme, Everything Comes to Dust, Winds of Abandon, Edgar Charmed Groom or Black Market Connections; for these the record is an inclusion rate and the oracle text only.

No fetchable primer describes a bracket-3 Edgar without any gain-to-loss loop piece; every list fetched runs Vito and/or Sanguine Bond, and most run Conqueror or Exquisite Blood. The pilot's thesis ('Vampires are the fuel, not the engine') has no published analogue; the Upgraded + Lifedrain filter is the closest and holds 87 decks.

Emeritus of Woe appears in EDHREC's average bracket-3 aristocrats 99 but is not in data/cards.csv (corpus refresh deferred 2026-11), so its identity and legality are unverified and it is not named in any finding.

Commander Spellbook results are truncated (count null, first page only); lines beyond the first eight per query are not recorded. Whether any of the branch's five contained lines works is a resolve-stack question, not a recon one.

No source measures what the pilot's thesis needs measured: the drain-per-death rate, the hand size after a wipe, or the clock without lords. Those are goldfish and Forge questions; recon can only say the strong lists do not build that way.
